results.title: Was TrafficTech-GH designed to raise revenue for gov’t? – Fiifi Boafo questions 60% share of fines
results.content: Former COCOBOD Director of Public Affairs, Fiifi Boafo, has questioned the government's decision to take 60 per cent of fines generated under the TrafficTech-GH system, suggesting that the arrangement raises concerns about whether the initiative is intended to improve road safety or generate revenue for the state.

results.title: Traffitech must not become government revenue tool at motorists’ expense – Fiifi Boafo
results.content: Former Head of Public Affairs at the Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD), Fiifi Boafo, has questioned the financial motive behind the introduction of the new automated traffic enforcement system, Traffitech, warning that it must not become a revenue-generating venture for the government rather than a road safety intervention.

results.title: Bright Simons questions TraffiTech-GH’s enforcement framework, warns of camera abuse and unlawful penalties
results.content: The Honorary Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons, has raised concerns about aspects of the TraffiTech-GH system, warning that its enforcement mechanisms could be abused and that some of the penalties being proposed may lack legal backing.

results.title: TraffiTech-GH: Viewing enforcement as revenue tool derails road safety efforts – Sharif Khalid
results.content: Economic Advisor to the Office of the Vice President, Sharif Mahmud Khalid, has cautioned against viewing the TraffiTech-GH automated traffic enforcement system primarily as a revenue-generating initiative, arguing that such an approach could undermine its road safety objectives.

results.title: MTTD addressing complaints over trade plates, vehicle ownership, data under new traffic system – ACP Alexander Obeng
results.content: The Police Motor Traffic and Transport Department (MTTD) says it is addressing complaints received within the first seven days of implementing the new automated traffic enforcement system, including concerns over trade licence plates, untransferred vehicle ownership and data discrepancies.

results.title: Good intentions not enough to guarantee success of TraffiTech-GH – Bright Simons
results.content: The Honorary Vice President of IMANI Africa, Bright Simons, says the success of the TraffiTech-GH initiative should be judged by how effectively it is implemented rather than the good intentions behind its introduction.

results.title: GES dismisses reports of student’s death at Ghana National College as old incident
results.content: The Ghana Education Service (GES) has dismissed reports suggesting that a student has died at Ghana National College, clarifying that the reported incident occurred in 2018.

results.title: TrafficTech-GH: Government must ensure clear speed limits, fair enforcement – Victoria Bright
results.content: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has called on the government to ensure clear road signage and fair enforcement under the TraffiTech-GH automated traffic management system, insisting that road safety and accountability must go hand in hand.

results.content: Only 18 per cent of countries in the World Health Organisation’s African Region have dedicated domestic funding for their health information systems, raising concerns about the sustainability of the data infrastructure used to guide health planning and service delivery. results.title: Fire destroys vulcanising shop at Dominase, ECG transformer salvaged
results.content: A fire has destroyed a vulcanising shop at Dominase in the Upper Denkyira West District of the Central Region, although personnel of the Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) managed to save a 1,500KVA transformer belonging to the Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG).

results.title: Nearly 60% of road fatalities linked to speeding, inattentive driving – NRSA
results.content: The Director of Regulations, Inspections and Compliance at the National Road Safety Authority (NRSA), Kwame Kodua Attuahene, says speeding and inattentive driving jointly account for approximately 58 to 59 per cent of road crash fatalities in Ghana.

results.title: TrafficTech, although good, is not backed by law – Lawyer
results.content: The Head of Chambers at Gyamfi Legal PRUC in Kumasi, Albert Gyamfi, says the newly implemented TraffiTech-GH system is illegal, saying that it lacks the necessary legal backing and unfairly imposes traffic fines on vehicle owners rather than the actual offenders.

results.title: Victoria Bright welcomes automated traffic enforcement system, says it is long overdue
results.content: Private legal practitioner Victoria Bright has welcomed the introduction of the new automated traffic enforcement system, describing it as a necessary and long-overdue intervention to help save lives on Ghana’s roads.

results.title: Tokenising government securities could attract more foreign investors to Ghana – WeWire CEO
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of WeWire, Ebenezer Ghanney, says tokenising Ghana's government securities could make it easier for international investors to access the domestic market and expand the government's sources of funding. He believes issuing digital tokens linked to government bonds and Treasury instruments could reduce some of the traditional barriers that make it difficult for foreign investors to participate in Ghana's financial market. Speaking at the Africa Virtual Assets Summit (AVSA) in Accra, Mr Ghanney identified government securities as among the financial products that could be relatively easy to tokenise because existing market structures and custody arrangements are already in place. “Government securities are easier because the product doesn't require heavy lifting like gold. With gold, we need to make sure that we have the custody sorted out,” he said.

results.title: Livestream: Newsfile discusses Traffitech-GH, drug busts and Parliament’s continued absence of Asante Akyem North MP
results.content: This Saturday’s edition of Newsfile on JoyNews will examine three major issues dominating Ghana’s public discourse, as host Samson Lardy Anyenini leads discussions on road safety enforcement, the fight against drug trafficking and developments in Parliament.

results.title: COP31: African negotiators target tripled adaptation finance and Green Climate Fund replenishment
results.content: The African Group of Negotiators on Climate Change (AGN) is placing climate adaptation finance at the forefront of its agenda as the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) opens in Antalya, Turkey, on November 9.

results.title: Sunyani Teaching Hospital needs staff accommodation to support expansion – CEO
results.content: The Chief Executive Officer of the Sunyani Teaching Hospital, Dr Cardinal Newton, has called on the government, private investors, and philanthropists to support the construction of staff accommodation to meet the facility’s growing demand.

results.title: Kow Abaka Essuman declares intention to contest Ablekuma West NPP parliamentary primary
results.content: Kow Abaka Essuman, former Legal Counsel to ex-President Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, has declared his intention to contest the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) parliamentary primary in the Ablekuma West Constituency.

results.title: Fire destroys Agbogba restaurant near Yellow Container
results.content: Firefighters on Friday, November 6, 2026, battled a fiercely spreading inferno that completely destroyed a restaurant near the popular Yellow Container landmark at Agbogba in Accra.

results.title: Zenith SME Business Empowerment Lab: SMEs urged to identify business risks and adopt mitigation strategies to ensure sustainability
results.content: According to the experts, business resilience goes beyond responding to crises. It requires a deliberate and strategic approach to identifying potential vulnerabilities, safeguarding critical operations and implementing contingency measures that enable businesses to adapt, recover and thrive in the face of disruptions

results.content: The Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr. Johnson Asiama, has strongly defended the decision by the Monetary Policy Committee to hold the policy rate at 14% between May and September 2026. results.title: ‘Days of diverting cocoa inputs are over’ – COCOBOD CEO
results.content: The Ghana Cocoa Board (COCOBOD) has issued a stern warning to individuals and officials involved in the diversion, hoarding or illegal sale of free fertiliser and other farm inputs, saying a new digital monitoring system will make it easier to identify and prosecute offenders.

results.title: William Frimpong-Bonsu enters Asutifi North NPP parliamentary race
results.content: William Frimpong-Bonsu, popularly known as Joe Willie, has declared his intention to contest the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) parliamentary primary in the Asutifi North Constituency of the Ahafo Region, pledging to champion party unity, effective representation and accelerated development.

results.title: Sons of the sound: How Mfanstsipim incubated and nurtured Ghana’s contemporary gospel
results.content: Contemporary gospel music emerged in Ghana in the early 1970s, marking a major development in the country’s Christian music. Churches had long used hymns, anthems, cantatas, indigenous songs and some western instruments, yet many conservative evangelicals still regarded rock, soul, disco and electric guitars as worldly.

results.title: Ghanaian singer Efya marries Nigerian star Tomi Thomas
results.content: Ghanaian singer Efya Nokturnal and Nigerian musician Tomi Thomas have formalised their union in a colourful traditional marriage ceremony in Accra, bringing together music, fashion and cultural traditions from both countries.

results.title: Ghana loses $6.5bn in potential mining revenue – IFS
results.content: The country loses an estimated $6.56 billion in potential revenue from the mining sector every year due to the government’s limited participation in mineral extraction, the Institute for Fiscal Studies (IFS) has revealed.

results.title: Man allegedly spends 3 days in cemetery coffin in suspected money ritual at Foase
results.content: A bizarre discovery at a cemetery in Foase in the Atwima Kwanwoma District of the Ashanti Region has left residents unsettled after a hunter reportedly found a 28-year-old drug store operator inside a coffin.

results.title: You entrust officials with $1m but pay them $400 – former Head of Civil Service slams salary structure
results.content: Former Head of the Civil Service, Dr Alex Glover-Quartey, has called for better remuneration for senior public servants, arguing that government cannot expect officials entrusted with millions of dollars in public funds to maintain high standards of integrity while paying them what he describes as inadequate salaries.

results.title: US Embassy explains how Ghanaians can secure emergency visa interviews
results.content: The United States Embassy in Accra has outlined the procedure for nonimmigrant visa applicants seeking an earlier interview because of an unexpected emergency, urging them to follow the required steps and provide evidence to support their requests.
